previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with a complex history including fibrosing mesenteritis, multiple abdominal surgeries, chronic TPN dependence, and recurrent line infections was admitted due to a positive blood culture for coagulase-negative staphylococcus from her PICC line. She remained clinically stable without fever or systemic signs of infection. The PICC line was removed, and subsequent cultures from the line tip and repeated blood draws were negative. Multiple attempts to place a new upper extremity central line failed due to venous stenoses and a non-occlusive thrombus in the right subclavian vein. A tunneled left femoral double-lumen central line was successfully placed for ongoing TPN. Infectious disease recommended further molecular testing to evaluate for a persistent source. The patient was discharged home with home health services to manage her line and nutrition, with follow-up arranged with her ID and GI specialists.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ year old female with complex medical history 
of mesenteric  
fibromatosis, multiple abdominal surgeries for SBO/pain, s/p 
venting g-tube and chronic indwelling femoral tunneled catheter 
that presented to the hospital with right sided chest pain after 
a few weeks of nausea and vomiting, found to have an anterior 
fifth rib fracture and a positive blood culture for enterococcus 
drawn from femoral catheter.

# Bacteremia:  Pt had one positive blood culture from ___ that 
was drawn from her chronic indwelling femoral catheter.  
Surveillance blood cultures drawn daily from her PIV and femoral 
catherter were all negative at the time of discharge.   She was 
started on daptomycin 500 mg q24 for empiric coverage of the 
enterococcus on ___ after consulting with ID.  Based on ID 
recs, an ethanol dwell in tunnelled femoral catheter was given 
for two hours prior to initiation of each daily session of TPN.  
This two hour dwell was later changed to vancomycin because of 
nationwide shortage of ethanol.  ID felt that the tunneled 
femoral catheter did not need to removed.  Final sensitivites 
returned on enterococcus on ___ and ID recommending sending pt 
home on daptomycin 500 mg q24 to complete a two week course 
(final day ___.

# Right chest wall pain:  Etiology of right chest wall pain is 
likely a combination of the rib fracture as well as strained 
intercostal muscles.  CT of the chest showed a subacute anterior 
fifth rib fracture, however her pain was located more superiorly 
and posterior than would be expected for corresponding rib 
fracture.  Fracture may have been related to the few prior weeks 
of nausea and vomiting. Her right chest wall pain decreased to 
an ___ when toradol was added to home morphine regimen.  
___ was d/c after two days out of concern for GI irritation.

# Chronic Pain Syndrome:  Pt continued to have abdominal pain 
during hospitalization that was consistent with baseline level.  


# Gastric dysmotility: Per recs from Dr. ___ felt that her 
increased G-tube output was likely related to obstruction, she 
was started on TPN on ___.  She was sent home on TPN through 
femoral catheter.

# Bilateral UE DVT:  Based on stable CTA chest, pt was continued 
on lovenox SC BID during hospitalization.

# Hypothyroidism: Pt was continued on levothyroxine 88 mcg po 
daily. 

Pt was sent home with provided services to complete course of 
daptomycin and vancomycin locks, in addition to continuation of 
TPN per nutrition recommendations.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ female with fibrosing mesenteritis, new right chest
pain and tachycardia.

___.

TECHNIQUE:  Helical MDCT images were acquired through the chest without and
with intravenous contrast, per the chest CTA protocol.  5- and 2.5-mm axial,
5-mm coronal and sagittal, and 3 mm bilateral oblique multiplanar reformats
were generated.

FINDINGS:  There is no main, branch, lobar, or segmental pulmonary embolus. 
The main pulmonary artery is enlarged at 3.5 cm, indicative of pulmonary
arterial hypertension.  The thoracic aorta is normal in caliber throughout. 
Heart is normal in size, with leftward bowing of the interventricular septum,
indicative of right heart strain.  Calcifications are noted in the left
anterior descending coronary artery.

The left brachiocephalic vein is chronically attenuated, with numerous left
chest wall and mediastinal venous collaterals, the majority of which drain
into the azygos vein.  

Sub-1-mm pulmonary nodules are present in the right upper lobe (2:19).  There
is no focal consolidation.  No pleural effusions are present.  Central airways
are patent to the subsegmental levels.

A prominent axillary node measures 7 mm in short axis, but demonstrates a
fatty hilum.  Mediastinal and hilar lymph nodes are not pathologically
enlarged.

Note is made of a small hiatal hernia.

Evaluation is not tailored for subdiaphragmatic evaluation, but reveals fatty
infiltration of the liver and chronic postoperative pneumobilia.

There is a mildly displaced fracture of the right anterior fifth rib.  Callus
formation is present, indicating subacute injury.  Nerve stimulator device is
present within the posterior spinal canal, spanning the T4-T8 levels. 
Abandoned lead is present in the right posterior soft tissues.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No PE.
2.  Subacute anterior fifth rib fracture.
3.  Pulmonary arterial hypertension.
4.  Chronic left brachiocephalic vein occlusion.
5.  Fatty liver.
6.  Chronic postoperative pneumobilia.
